outcome: A mana ability or spell effect adds mana to the controller's pool, with the ability's source as the mana's source.
Added mana sits in the pool, can pay costs, and is lost when the pool empties at the end of each step and phase.
An ability that would produce mana of an undefined type produces no mana.
Restricted mana can be spent only as its restriction allows, and its riders or delayed triggers apply when spent, without changing its type.
A replacement effect that increases mana produced applies the source's restrictions and additional effects to every mana, with one delayed trigger per mana.
An ability based on mana a permanent could produce yields the types its abilities would produce at that time, or no mana if none.
Hybrid mana added to a pool becomes one mana of the chosen half's color or the chosen generic amount of colorless mana.
Phyrexian mana added to a pool is one mana of the symbol's color.
Generic mana symbols add that much colorless mana.
Snow mana symbols add that much colorless mana.
A 'tapped for mana' trigger fires when the mana ability resolves and produces mana of the specified type.
A 'tapped for mana' replacement effect modifies the mana production event while the ability resolves.
Drain Power empties one player's pool and adds the same mana, with restrictions intact, to the other player's pool.
